prompt.es: Escribe un artículo de opinión (130–250 palabras) y termina con «Revision:».

answer.text: Should students have a say in the school rules? In this piece I will argue that they should. First, rules that nobody explains are rarely followed. When students help to write a rule, they understand the reason for it, and they respect it more. Second, taking part teaches responsibility. A student who helps to decide learns that every choice has consequences. I concede that students may not always choose the best rules. Nevertheless, teachers can guide the discussion, and, as mentioned above, a rule with a clear reason is easier to accept. This argument is stronger than the objection, because guided choices are still choices. Teachers and students want different things: the former want order, and the latter want fairness. A shared rule can give both. In conclusion, students deserve a voice in the rules they must follow, and the school will be calmer for it. Revision: I cut a repeated sentence and replaced due to the fact that with because.

A shared rule can give both. In conclusion, students deserve a voice in the rules they must follow, and the school will be calmer for it. Do students deserve a say in school rules? I believe they do, and in this piece I will argue it. First, a rule that nobody explains is rarely followed, so students should know why it exists. Second, helping to make rules teaches responsibility, because a student learns that choices have consequences. Admittedly, some students will not choose wisely; nevertheless, teachers can guide them, and, as mentioned above, a clear reason makes any rule easier to accept. This argument answers the objection. Teachers and students often want different things: the former want order, and the latter want fairness, and a shared rule can give both. To sum up, schools should give students a voice, and the result will be a calmer and fairer place. Revision: I changed a long sentence into a shorter one and removed a repeated word.

feedback.es: Un artículo completo declara la tesis, desarrolla dos argumentos, concede y responde, enlaza con referencias internas, concluye y documenta la revisión.

origin.text: Revista del colegio: «¿Deben los estudiantes opinar sobre las normas?». Escribe un artículo de 130–250 palabras con tesis, dos argumentos, una concesión con su respuesta, una referencia interna (as mentioned above, this argument, the former/the latter) y una conclusión. Termina con una línea que empiece por «Revision:» y describa un cambio que hiciste al revisar (recortar o aclarar una referencia).
